timeline: Verified what an Artifact page can and can't do, found that this environment blocks the job-board APIs, and found a reachable real data source. Renamed the app from Ghosted to Heardback.
Design system (Geist, cool neutrals, one cobalt accent, full dark mode), app shell, command palette, local-first store, nudges engine, data pipeline with ghost signals, competitor scan.
Four agents built Find, Pipeline, Today/Insights and Prep/Onboarding/Settings in parallel. First publish.
Add to calendar (Google Calendar connector or .ics), email parser accuracy, core fixes.
Design review 1 scored 6.3. Removed noise everywhere. QA found 32 bugs; fixed every crash and broken feature.
Review 2 scored 7.4. Calmer layouts, tablet breakpoints, rounds as summaries. New: posting-taken-down detection, season-closing nudges, PDF resumes, new since your last visit.
Mock interview with Claude, bulk actions, command palette context actions, How we score listings.
Review 3 scored 8.1. One vocabulary for signals, softer selection, simpler mock interview. Share-your-progress card.
Review 4 scored 8.6. Quieter fit and freshness, typography, raised dark overlays. QA round 2 (2,280 checks): no crash or broken-feature bugs left.

An agent played a stressed intern-hunting student through 8 real tasks. Fixed: silence counted from the applied date, change-date on apply, confirm-your-interview task, ghost signals hidden by default with an honest count, onboarding survives reloads, mobile quick add.
CSV import preview with stage mapping, stage-aware nudges after interviews, strict level and location matching, US-only Remote, two-line mobile count bar, wrapping toasts.
Design review 6 scored 9.0. Zero axe-core WCAG 2 A/AA violations on every route and overlay in both themes. Silence respects scheduled rounds; share card opens on a meaningful period.

A student five weeks in with 42 applications. Today grouped into Today / Quick wins / When you have time, one row per application, batch ghosting, inline outcomes; J/K everywhere; Online assessment rounds; takedown callouts; age-matched Insights.
Review 7 (8.8) said the new UI was loud. One focus style, folded silent apps, two-button outcomes, one block for taken-down postings. End-to-end suite 2,428 / 2,428.

A cold-visitor test (someone tapping a LinkedIn link) and review 8. Degree-aware fit (PhD-only roles no longer top the list), fit only once skills exist, a one-glance first screen, Just browse jobs, See a sample tracker, an honest note for non-tech students.
Natural round names, last-reply agrees everywhere, Review instead of Apply on strong-ghost listings, distinct second follow-up.
Generic round type renamed Interview, browse-only visitors see no goal they never set, thin company stats hidden, Interviews get their own color. 1,900 random clicks and keys: zero errors.

A fourth usability test walked through interview day. A Next up row pins the next round with Open notes and Join; rounds get a Where field filled from invite emails; Prep shows your notes on the company; mock answers and practice outlines save to notes; honest calendar states.
Final design check (9.2, ship) fixes; job data refreshed at 7:30 AM; end-to-end 2,428 / 2,428, axe clean, zero console errors at every width and theme.
qa: Every published version passed Playwright runs at 375, 768 and 1440 px in light and dark mode with zero console errors and no horizontal overflow. The end-to-end suite drives the real UI (onboarding, search, saving, drag and drop, keyboard, bulk actions, email logging with 11 realistic emails, rounds, nudges, Insights math, export/import round-trips, corrupt data, 300 applications, focus and Escape behavior) at phone and desktop widths, with and without Claude: __CHECKS__ checks, all passing in the final run. An axe-core scan finds zero WCAG 2 A/AA violations on every screen and overlay in both themes. Three usability tests (an intern hunter on desktop, a new grad on a phone, a power user with 42 applications) drove the last rounds of fixes.

post_main:
[Edit to your own experience] Half the internship listings I applied to last year never replied. Some of them were never real.

So I built Heardback, a free job search app for internships and new-grad roles that asks one question about every listing: will you actually hear back?

• 7,500+ live internship and new-grad roles, each linking straight to the company's own application page
• A ghost-job check on every listing, with the reasons: how long it's been up, how many times it was closed and reposted, how many cities it's blasted across
• A pipeline that tracks every interview round. Paste a recruiter email and it logs itself.
• A Today view that tells you who to follow up with, when a posting was taken down, and when to call it ghosted
• Mock interviews and prep for each round, on your own Claude account

It's free and your data stays in your browser.

If you're recruiting this season, try it and log your last 10 applications.
